proceedings before the tribunal, leading to ex-parte orders, but at the stage of certificate proceedings, they appear before the
tribunal and pray for the setting aside ex-parte orders on flimsy grounds. The Committee has, therefore, proposed that there
should be provision in the Act/Rules that if the tribunal is satisfied and decides to set aside ex-parte order, then the order
should be made subject to payment of 50% of the certificate amount. The Working Group in para 2.14 of the report, has
recommended that it should be the duty of the applicant bank/financial institution to ensure that the due service is effected on
the borrower. Once the lending banks/institutions take interest in effecting service of notices on their borrowers, the
borrower is unlikely to remain absent from the proceedings and in spite of the proper service on him, he chooses not to
participate in the proceedings and the ex-parte order is passed by the tribunal, the tribunals should avoid entertaining requests
for setting aside such ex-parte order is passed by the tribunal, the tribunals should avoid entertaining requests for setting
aside such ex-parte orders unless very cogent reasons are shown by the borrower/defendant why he could not participate in
the proceedings on the notified date. In such a case, in the opinion of the Working Group, it should be left to the discretion of
the PO of DRTs to decide whether to set aside such ex-parte order and if so, subject to what terms. However, it will not be
proper to curtail the discretion of the PO by providing payment of 50% of the certificate amount of setting aside such ex-
parte order.

   Ministry’s comments : (12.5. 2004)
In case of contravention of any provisions of the SEBI Regulations, four options are available, namely: -

Time limit to be specified within which Chairman/Member to pass the order.

167th Report of Committee on Subordinate Legislation
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/167thReport.htm[25-10-2016 16:44:04]
        Ministry’s comments: (12.5 2004)
The corresponding provisions in earlier Regulations provided for a time limit of 30 days from the hearing date within
which the Chairman would have to pass orders.  In two cases, where the order could not be passed within the said limit, SAT
held that if the order is not passed within the stipulated time, then in such cases Chairman/Member becomes functus officio
and thereafter no order can be passed.  Therefore, the amendment has been made to provide for passing the order ‘as soon as
possible’ so that the intermediary shall not escape penalty on mere technicalities.  Though it is desirable, it is not always
possible to adhere to a rigid time limit within which the Chairman/Member should pass the order in view of the various
technicalities and peculiarities which may be present in a particular case.  Some cases require further inquiries/investigation
in view of the submissions of the party or may require appreciation of voluminous evidence.  Some may involve complicated
questions of law on which legal opinion may have to be taken.  In some other cases, the order is not being able to be passed
on account of litigation pending before Courts/Tribunals.  Therefore, it is felt that a rigid time limit which may lead to non-
compliant orders being treated as non est in law may seriously jeopardize regulatory efforts in such cases.
It is further felt that such time limits are not mentioned in any relevant regulatory statutes.  Even in respect of
adjudications by Adjudication Officers of SEBI, section 151(2) of the SEBI Act, 1992 read with rule 5(1) of the SEBI
(Procedure for Holding Inquiry by Adjudication Officers and Imposing Penalty) Rules, 1995 do not specify any time limit
within which the Adjudication Officer should pass the order imposing monetary penalty.  Even in respect of original
regulatory adjudications under other statutes, no provisions are found wherein time limits have been stipulated for passing of
orders.  An example is section 13 of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 read with rule 4(8) of the Foreign
Exchange Management (Adjudicating and Appeals) Rules, 2000 which merely say that the Adjudicating Authority can by
order, impose appropriate penalty.  Similar were the provisions under section 50 of the erstwhile Foreign Exchange
Regulation Act, 1973 read with rule 3 of the Adjudication Proceedings and Appeal Rules, 1974.  Section 11AC of the
Central Excise Act, 1944 read with rules 25 to 27 of the Central Excise Rules, 2002 and section 122 of the Customs Act,
1962 also do not contain any time limit for passing an order of imposition of penalty or confiscation of goods.
     Committee’s observation :(7.2.2005)
The Committee noted that SEBI had accepted its suggestion to find out a via-media and amended the regulations
appropriately with regarding prescription of time limit for passing order by the Chairman/ Member.
     Action Taken by the Ministry (7.6.2005)
The Ministry have notified the amendment as suggested by the Committee.

have amended Rules 4 by adding a new sub rule (3) which places an obligation upon the SPCBs and PCCs to collect, compile and
publish technical and statistical data in consultation with the CPCB relating to noise pollution and measure devised for its effective
prevention, control and abatement. The Committee feels that this would result in better and effective implementation of the rules.
            The Committee further notes with satisfaction that Government have amended rules 8 as well thereby providing an
opportunity to the complainant also to be heard while the Authority regulating noise levels reviews its orders based inter- alia on a
complaint, as suggested by it.
*****
Summary of Recommendations
 
I
 
The Committee considered the position as furnished by the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pension vide
their O.M. dated the 15th April, 2005 and noted that the matter had already been settled through judicial pronouncement. The
Committee also considered the background of the matter, the judicial pronouncements on the subject and the implication of
implementing the Committee’s recommendations as pointed out by the Ministry and decided not to pursue the
recommendation as contained in the 117
th Report.
II
 
The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Company Affairs have carried out and notified all the
amendments in Cost Accounting Records ( Electricity Industry) Rules , 2001as recommended by it.
 
III
 
            The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Finance have since published the Customs House Agents
Licensing (First Amendment) Regulations, 2005 vide notification No G.S.R.653 (E) dated the 7
th November, 2005
(Annexure) carrying out the recommendations of the Committee as follows:
 Point 9 (Regulations 8(7)): By omitting the words "an additional or ", thereby making Hindi a desirable qualification
instead of " an additional or desirable" qualification in case a person is to be deputed to work exclusively in the dock.

2.         During the course of scrutiny of these Orders, the Committee has noted some cases where there has been a considerable time
lag between the date of notification of the Order and the date of its laying. The annexed statement also indicates the period of delay in
cases where notifications have not been laid as per the schedule prescribed by the Committee and whether such notifications were
accompanied by a statement indicating the reasons for the delay in laying. In some of the cases the delay has been quite long. The
observations/recommendations of the Committee in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments are as follows: -  
           
(i) Ministry of Agriculture (Department of Agriculture Research and   Education)
 
            The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of five months in laying one notification (Sl. No. 01) and no delay
statement was sent therewith. The Committee would like the Ministry of Agriculture (Department of Agriculture Research and  
Education) to take corrective measures so as to obviate such delay in future.
 
(ii) Ministry of Agriculture (Department of Animal Husbandry, Dairying and Fisheries)
 
      The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of seven months on the part of the Ministry of Agriculture
(Department of Animal Husbandry, Dairying and Fisheries) in laying two of their notifications (Sl. Nos. 6 & 7). In both these cases
the Ministry have failed to append the delay statement. The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Agriculture (Department of Animal
Husbandry, Dairying and Fisheries) would avoid delay in laying of the notifications and in case of any delay actually taking place in
laying, a delay statement would invariably be appended.
 
(iii) Ministry of Defence
 
      The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Defence have delayed the laying of one of their notification (Sl. No. 38) by
five months.  The Ministry have appended delay statement with the Notification and the reasons given by the Ministry reads: “The
delay in laying the papers has occurred due to inadvertent omission on the part of officer in the Naval Headquarters dealing with the
case. There was also a change in the officers dealing with the case. However, instructions have been reiterated to all the Departments
and Offices under the Ministry of Defence to ensure that notification etc. required to be laid on the table of the Parliament are sent to
Parliament Secretariat in time.”
       The Committee hopes that the action taken by the Ministry would avoid recurrence of such instances in future.
(iv) Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs)
 
            The Committee regrets to note that there has been delay up to 10 months in the laying of two notifications (Sl. Nos. 48 & 82). 
The Ministry have not appended delay statement with the notification at Sl. No. 48.  The delay statement appended with the
Notification at Sl. No. 48 reads : “ The Copies of the Gazette Notification No. ADVT-III/IV/23-E/2006/Exty. Dated 2
nd May, 2006
containing Rajasthan Gramin Bank (Officers & Employees) Service Regulations, 2006 could not be laid on the Table of the Rajya as
the copies of Service Regulations of Rajasthan Gramin Bank, were received on 24 th November, 2006. The notification is now being
laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha during current Session of Parliament.” The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Finance
(Department of Economic Affairs) should stick to the time schedule as recommended by it in its 131st Report in the matter of laying of
Subordinate Legislation before Parliament and that they should review their internal mechanism so that the copies of the notifications
are received on time and this does not become the cause for delay in laying papers before the Parliament.
 
(v) Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue)
 
            The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) have delayed the laying of three
notifications (Sl Nos. 91, 92 & 93) laid by them. The delay statement appended with the Notification at Sl. No. 91 reads: “The Copies
of the Gazette Notification No. ADVT. III/.IV/ 253G/2005/Exty., dated 10
th March, 2006 containing Jaipur Thar Gramin Bank
(Officers & Employees) Service Regulations, 2006 could not be laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha as the copies of Service
Regulations of Jaipur Thar Gramin Bank, were received in the month of September, 2006. The notification is now being laid on the
Table of the Rajya Sabha during Winter Session of Parliament.” Similar delay statements have been also appended with the
Notifications at Sl. Nos. 92 & 93. The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) would avoid such
instances in future and that the Ministry would take necessary corrective measures to avoid delay in laying on such grounds and
adhere to the schedule prescribed by the Committee in its 131st Report. .

(vi) Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (Department of Health)
          The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of upto 12 and 5 months on the part of the Ministry of Health &
Family Welfare (Department of Health) in laying two of their notifications laid by them (Sl. No.117 & 118). The delay statement
appended with the Notification at Sl. No. 117 states :-“Since the provisions of these Rules are subjudice in the matter of Mahesh Bhatt
Vs Union of India pending before the High Court of Delhi, the same could not be laid on the Table of both Houses of Parliament in
time. Further, these rules have been further amended by “The Cigarettes and other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement
and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) (Amendment) Rules, 2006” which was notified in the
gazette of India vide GSR No. 656 (E) dated 20.10.2006. These provisions are yet to come into force. The said notifications are now
proposed to be laid on the Table of both the Houses in the current Session of the Parliament.”
      The delay statement appended with Notification at Sl. No. 118 reads:
      “ Since the requisite number of copies of printed notification were not received in time, the same could not be laid on the Table of
both Houses of Parliament in time. The said notification is now proposed to be laid on the Table of both the Houses in the current
Session of the Parliament.” The  Committee is not convinced with the grounds for delay put forth by the Ministry in case of
Notification at Sl. No. 118. The fact that an existing Subordinate Legislation is being considered for change is no ground for delaying
the laying of the same before the Parliament. Similarly, inadequate number of copies of notifications is a very common ground for
delay in laying. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Department of Health) should take
necessary corrective steps so that such instances do not recur.  
 
(vii) Ministry of Home Affairs
            The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Home Affairs have delayed by eight months the laying of their
notification (Sl. No. 129). The Ministry have not appended any delay statement with the said notification. The Committee hopes that
the Ministry of Home Affairs would avoid such instances of delay in the laying of Subordinate Legislation and shall in such
circumstance keep the House informed of the reasons for delay in laying by appending delay statements. 
 
(viii) Ministry of Human Resource Development (Department of Higher Education)
The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Human Resource Development (Department of Higher Education) have
delayed in laying one of their notification (Sl. No. 137) by two months. No delay statement has been appended with the said
notification.. The Committee expects the Ministry of Human Resource Development (Department of Higher Education) to exercise
caution in the matter of timely laying of subordinate legislation and ensure that such delays do not recur and in case of any delay
actually taking place, a delay statement is invariably  appended while laying the notification.
 
(ix) Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions (Department of Personnel and Training)
The Committee regrets to note that one Notification (Sl. No. 152) laid by the Department of Personnel and Training of the
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions has been delayed by 17 months. No delay statement has been appended with
the said notification.  The Committee regrets to note that the Department of Personnel and Training have abnormally delayed the
laying of their notification and at the same time, the Parliament have not been apprised of the reasons for such delay. The Committee
invites attentions of the Ministry towards the Committee’s recommendations on the subject reproduced at the end of this report, for
their strict compliance.
 
(x) Ministry of Power
 
            The Committee regrets to note that one Notification (Sl. No.165) laid by the Ministry of Power has been delayed by eight
months. The Ministry have appended delay statement with the said Notification and it reads : “Copies of the above Notification were
forwarded by the Central Electricity Authority on 16.11.2006 for laying down on the table of Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha. Delay in laying
down the Regulations occurred in view of the fact that this is the first of the Regulations made by CEA under the Electricity Act,
2003. CEA has been asked to avoid such delay in future.”
 
            The Committee hopes that the Ministry would avoid such instances of delay in laying of Subordinate Legislation in future.
 
 
3.     The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take immediate steps to ensure timely and proper laying of
subordinate legislation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Departments of the Government of
India, particularly, the defaulting ones, the following recommendations, as contained in its 131
st,135th  and 152nd Reports:
        “Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session immediately
following the date of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, on the date of the publication
of the Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between the date of publication and the date of the closing of the Session
is less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said Session. All the Ministries/Departments of
Government of India should henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of the Orders issued under various Acts of
Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.”  (131
st Report)

Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules-2002
 
            
The Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002 framed under the Securitisation & Reconstruction of Financial Assets &
Enforcement of Security Interest Ordinance, 2002 were examined and a questionnaire was forwarded to the Ministry of Finance (Banking
Division) on the 24 th November, 2003, to which the Ministry replied on the 7 th May, 2004. The Committee considered the Ministry’s
reply at its meeting held on 17 th November, 2005 and decided to seek further clarification on point No.1 (Rule 2 (d) defining ‘Approved
Valuer’). The Ministry vide their communication dated 29th November, 2006 provided the requisite clarification and also gave details of
the changes carried out by the Ministry on the other points on Committee’s suggestion.
 
2.         The points referred to the Ministry, their comments/clarifications and their Action Taken on each point are reproduced below: -
 
1.         Point raised- Rule 2(d) -
“Approved valuer” means a valuer as approved by the Board of Directors or Board of Trustees of the secured creditor, as the case
may be.
Should the approved valuer not be duly qualified; what is the justification for giving full discretion to the secured creditor in this
regard?
 
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
Approved valuer means the professional who is qualified to value the property for a fee.  It is difficult to work out clear-cut
definition making exhaustive list of approved valuers in different fields and types of properties that are to be valued.   It is, however,
suggested that banks and financial institutions may be advised to utilize the services of valuers through Institution of Valuers who
claimed to be the only registered body in the country and their members are bound by code of conduct prescribed by it.  They are covered
by fee prescribed by the Government under Rule 8C of the Wealth Tax Act and also by CBDT.
 
Action Taken by the Ministry : (29.11.2006)
In terms of Rule 8(5) of Security Enforcement Rules, 2002, before effecting sale of immovable property, the authorized officer is
required to obtain valuation of the property from an approved valuer and in consultation with the secured creditor, fix the reserve price of
the property.  Chapter VII-B (Section 34 AB) of Wealth Tax Act, 1957 provides for registration of valuers.  Any person who possesses
the qualifications prescribed under Rule 8A of Wealth Tax Rules, 1957, may apply to the Chief Commissioner or Director General for
being registered as a valuer under the Wealth Tax Act, 1957.  In terms of Rule 8A ibid, different qualifications have been prescribed for
valuers of different classes of assets (like for agricultural land, for plantations, for forests, for mines & quarries, for plant and machinery,
for immovable property other than agricultural land, plantations etc.).  We may not have objection in suitably modifying the definition of
Approved Valuer, “to mean a person registered as a valuer under Section 34 AB of Wealth Tax Act, 1957 and approved by the Board of
Directors or Board of Trustees of the secured creditor, as the case may be”.

169th Report of Committee on Subordinate Legislation
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/169threport.htm[25-10-2016 16:42:52]
 
2.         Point raised- Rule 4(1)
Where the possession of the secured assets to be taken by the secured creditor are movable property in possession of the borrower,
the authorized officer shall take possession of such movable property in the presence of two witnesses after a Panchanama drawn and
signed by the witnesses as nearly as possible in Appendix-I to these rules
Are these two witnesses, the witnesses, of the secured creditor or they are the public/independent witnesses; should the rule not
clarify on this point?
 
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
Witnesses could be any one.  Flexibility in this matter is desirable and is recognized by the legislation as well as judiciary.   No
clarification in the Rule is necessary, as the present provision does not confine witnesses to specific classes of persons.
 
3.         Point raised- Rule 4(3)
The authorized officer shall keep the property taken possession under sub-rules (1) either in his own custody or in the custody of
any person authorized or appointed by him, who shall take as much care of the property in his custody as an owner of ordinary prudence
would, under the similar circumstances, take of such property.
                                   
 
This rule involves further delegation of power by the authorized officer to any person authorized or appointed by him without
fixing any responsibility either to the authorized officer or the person so authorized or appointed by him in case there is any damage to
the movable property in custody inadvertently.   Should the rule not vest ultimate responsibility on the authorised officer even in case
where he has authorized some body in this behalf?
 
Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
In terms of Rule 4(3), the Authorised Officer shall take as much care of the property in his custody as owner of ordinary
prudence.  Further as per Rule 4(4), the Authorised Officer shall take steps for preservation and protection of secured assets and insure
them, if necessary, till they are sold or otherwise disposed of.  Therefore even though the Authorised Officer is empowered to entrust the
possession to others; he is still responsible for acts of the custodian appointed by him to keep the assets.  Moreover, in terms of Section 19
of the Act, if the DRT or DRAT holds the possession of secured assets by the secured creditor as wrongful and directs the secured
creditor to return such assets to the borrower, such borrower shall be entitled to payment of such compensation and costs as may be
determined by the DRT or DRAT.  Hence, no specific provision, as contemplated by the Committee is necessary.
 
4.         Point raised- Rule 5
Valuation of movable secured assets: After taking possession under sub-rule (1) of the Rule 4 and in any case before
sale, the authorized officer shall obtain the estimated value of the movable secured assets and thereafter, if considered
necessary, fix in consultation with the secured creditor, the reserve price of the assets to be sold in realization of the dues of
the secured creditor.
While the rule envisages consultation with the secured creditor; why the borrower is not involved at all in fixing the reserve price
of the assets to be sold in realization of the dues of the secured creditor?
 
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
In the light of the Supreme Court observations in Haryana Financial Corporation V.Jagadamba (2002) 110 Comp. Case 20 (SC),
notice of intended sale to the defaulting borrower is sufficient and any procedure requiring the defaulting borrower to be associated or
consulted in every stage in the sale of secured assets will place unnecessary restrictions in the exercise of the powers vested with the
secured creditors.  Further, in terms of Rule 6(1), the Authorised Officer is expected to secure the maximum sale price of the property to
be sold.
 
5.         Point raised- Rule 6(3)
Sale by any methods other than public auction or public tender, shall be on such terms as may be settled between the parties in
writing.
Shouldn’t the settlement between the parties before being finalized be conveyed to the borrower; Secondly should the terms
settled between the parties not be required to be kept open for the sake of transparency?
 
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
As at 4 above.  To add, the Rules 6 and 9 provide for sufficient transparency of the transactions of sale.  The authorized officer is
expected to secure the maximum sale price and shall serve to the borrower a notice of thirty days for sale of secured assets including
public notice in Newspapers in case of public auction or invitation of tenders from public.   Further, borrower or secured creditor is not
prohibited from participation in the sale process, i.e. he can bid and purchase the secured assets.
 
6.         Point raised- Rule 8(2)
The possession notice as referred to in sub-rule (1) shall also be published in two leading newspapers, one in vernacular

language having sufficient circulation in that locality, by the authorized officer.
The rules does not specify within how much period of taking over possession of the property the possession notice shall be
published in the newspaper; Whether Government have any objection in prescribing about this aspect in the rules?
 
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
In view of the last para of the Appendix IV prescribing the form of the possession notice to the borrower and possession notice in
two leading newspapers for the public in general for cautioning against dealing with such property, these notices are required to be given
simultaneously.  For clarity purpose, this can be considered to be provided for it in the Rule.

The Notice regarding taking over the possession of the property should be issued as soon as possible but not later than 7 days from

“The possession notice as referred to in sub-rule (1) shall also be published as soon as possible but in any case not later than 7
days from the date of taking possession, in two leading newspapers, one in vernacular language having sufficient circulation in that
locality, by the authorized officer.”

provision, as contemplated by the Committee is necessary.

The authorized officer shall take steps for preservation and protection of secured assets and insure them, if necessary
till they are sold or otherwise disposed off.
Can the Authorised Officer not be made responsible for preservation and protection of secured assets rather then
merely saying that he shall “take steps”?

In terms of second proviso to sub-rule (2) of Rule 9, if the Authorised office fails to obtain a price higher than the reserve price, he

contingencies of further cost, expenses and interest without any approval or control of either the Board of Directors of the secured
creditor; should there not be some checks to avoid its misuse?
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
(a ) The person, who purchases the property, takes it subject to the subsequent encumbrances, if any, it possess, with the full
knowledge thereof.  Hence, if he desires to have the property free of encumbrance, he shall take steps to get the encumbrance discharged. 
This is, therefore, an enabling provision.  Also, it may be noted that in terms of sub-Rules (8) to (10), the authorized officer, who received
the payment to the party entitled to the payment pursuant to release of encumbrance, deliver property free of encumbrance (known to the
secured creditor) to the purchaser and issue sale certificate indicating the sale free of any encumbrance known to the secured.  Thus, it is
the choice of the purchase to purchase the property subject to encumbrance or free of encumbrance.
(b ) The suggestion of the Committee can be considered i.e. to provide for approval of the secured creditor as to the
additional amount required from the purchaser to discharge the subsequent encumbrance.
 
Action Taken by the Ministry : (29.11.2006)
The authorized officer is a responsible officer who will discharge his functions strictly in accordance with law.  When a property
is sold subject to any encumbrances, there may be some expenditure to discharge the encumbrances and to meet contingencies of further
costs.  The authorized officer must have the discretion to determine the amount.   To make such determination subject to the approval of
the Board of Directors or the Board of Trustees would only mean further delay and adding another layer of decision making to what is a
normal administrative matter.  Government is of the view that there is no need to add a layer of approval by the Board of Directors or the
Board of Trustees in order to check possible misuse.  If, in any case, misuse is brought to the notice of the Board of Directors or the
Board of Trustees, they could always revise the order of the authorized officer or take suitable action against him.  We should not add
more and more layers to decision making in what are purely administrative matters.   The only safeguard that we may add to Rule 9(7) is
making a proviso that if any money remains unspent out of the deposit made by the purchaser, after meeting the cost of removing
encumbrances and contingencies, that amount shall be returned to the purchaser.  It is therefore, suggested that following proviso may be
added below sub-rule (7) of Rule 9.
“Provided that if after meeting the cost of removing encumbrances and contingencies there is any surplus available out of the
money deposited by the purchaser such surplus shall be paid to the purchaser within 15 days from the date of finalisation of the sale”

The Board of Directors or the Board of  Trustees, as the case may be, may appoint in consultation with the borrower

(a)       The suggestion of the Committee may be accepted for a limited extent of consultation.  Association, in the sense of his approval,

(b)       The suggestion of the Committee can be considered.   The qualifications, as prescribed in sub-section (1) (b) (i) of section 10 of

Sub-Section (1)(b) (i) of the Section 10 of the B.R.Act specifies that a banking company shall not employ or continue the
employment of any person who is, or at any time, has been adjudicated insolvent, or has suspended payment or has compounded with his
creditors, or who is, or has been convicted by a Criminal Court of an offence involving moral turpitude.   Other than the above no
qualification has been prescribed to be appointed as “Manager”.
The Rule may read as follows:
Rule 10(1)
“The Board of Directors or the Board of Trustees, as the case may be, may appoint in consultation with the borrower any person

(hereinafter referred to as the Manager) to manage the secured assets the possession of which has been taken over by the secured creditor.
“Provided that the Manager so appointed shall not be a person who is, or at any time has been, adjudicated insolvent, or has

17.       Point raised- Rule 10(2)
The Manager appointed by the Board of Directors or Board of Trustees, as the case may be, shall be deemed to be an
agent of the borrower and the borrower shall be solely responsible for the commission or omission of acts of the Manager
unless such commission or omission are due to improper intervention of the secured creditor or the authorized officer.
The Manager is appointed only in consultation with the borrower and seemingly he is not exercising any control over him.  In
such a case fixing the sole responsibility for the acts of commission or omission of Manager on the borrower seems to be unreasonable;
what are the documents of Ministry in this behalf?

Although the Manager is appointed by the secured creditor to manage these secured assets, the possession of which is already
taken by the secured creditor, the secured creditor continues to be the mortgage only and the ownership remains with the borrower.  
However, since the control over the property passes with the possession to the secured creditor for realization of dues, very little control
remains with the borrower to deal with the property.  Hence, there is a merit in the suggestion of the Committee, particularly when only
consultation and not approval of the borrower is required for appointment of a manager.  Hence, the provision need reconsideration.
           
Action Taken by the Ministry : (29.11.2006)
The Rules as it stands, carves out an exception where any acts of omission or commission are due to the improper intervention of
the secured creditor or the authorized officer and in such a case the borrower is not responsible.  The provisions contained in sub rule (2)
of rule 10 are on the lines of the provisions contained in sub section (3) of section 69A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882.  The said
section was inserted by an amendment Act 20 of 1929 and the Government is of the view that there is no need to change the existing
provision.

An application for recovery of balance amount by any secured creditor pursuant to sub-section (10) of Section 13 of
the Ordinance shall be presented to the Debts Recovery Tribunal in the form annexed as Appendix VI to these rules by the

jurisdiction his case falls or shall be sent by registered post addressed to the Registrar of Debts Recovery Tribunal.
It has not been stated specifically in the rule as to who will appoint the duly authorized legal practitioner?
 
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
An application for recovery of balance amount by any secured creditor shall be presented by authorized legal practitioner or
authorized officer or his agent.  Hence, only the secured creditor can appoint the legal practitioner.

Delhi Advocates' Welfare Fund Rules, 2001.
 
            The Delhi Advocates' Welfare Fund Rules, 2001 framed under the Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 2001 were examined
and a questionnaire on the subject was forwarded to the Ministry of Law & Justice (Department of Legal Affairs) on the 17 th
January, 2003 for furnishing their comments. The Ministry vide  their communication dated the 12 th May, 2005 furnished their
comments.
 
            The Committee considered the subject matter at its meeting held on 24th October, 2005. The points raised and Ministry's
comments are as follows: -
 
1)         Point referred (Rule 9(8) )-
 
"The Chairperson or the person presiding over a meeting shall have and exercise a second or a casting vote in all cases of
equality of votes."
Would it not be more appropriate if the Chairman does not exercise voting right in the normal course but votes only to
remove the tie?
            Ministry's Comments (12.05.05):-
The suggestion that the Chairman, who exercises the voting right only to remove the tie, is appreciated. The casting vote
in all cases of equality appears to be vague.
2)         Point referred (Rule 9(12) )-
 
"Meeting of the Trustee Committee shall, ordinarily, be held at its Office."
 
            The word 'ordinarily' used in the Regulation appears to be vague. Under what circumstances, meeting of the Committee
may be held at the places other than its office?        
Ministry's Comments (12.05.05):-
            The Rule as it exists appears to be in order. Of course, it impliedly gives the power to hold the meeting at any other place
other than its office if it is not ordinarily possible to hold the meeting at its office.
 
3)         Point referred (Rule 12(1) )-
 
"The Bar Council of Delhi may issue a certificate of recognition in Form IV, after such enquiry as it deems necessary, on
the application, made under Rule II."
            Rule 12(2
)- "The Bar Council of Delhi may recognize more than one association of advocates functioning at a particular
court, tribunal or other authority."
            Rule 12(3
)- "The Bar Council of Delhi shall prepare list of recognized association of advocates and update the same
from time to time."
 
(a)        Whether the Ministry have any objection in prescribing a specific time period within which certificate for recognition
may be issued to the association of advocates.
(b)        There is no provision in the rule for appeal/review if the application for recognition is rejected. The Ministry may please
comment.
            Ministry's Comments (12.05.05):-
(a) A period of four months initially may be prescribed for issuing a certificate for recognition.
(b) It would be appropriate if appeal can be prescribed, for which adjudicating authority may be the State Bar Council of
each State.
 
 
4)         Point referred (Rule 13(2))-
 
 "An advocate having membership in more than one association of advocates shall so apply from any one of them."
Why Rule 13(2) contemplates membership of more than one association of advocates, when an advocate can apply only
through one association? Should the rules not prohibit membership of more than one association by an advocate?
            Ministry's Comments (12.05.05):-
            The Rule appears to be clear that an advocate can apply from any one of the associations. The Rule appears to be
reasonable and requires no change.
 
 
5)         Point referred (Rule 14)
-

Point-3: Regulation 4.4 (iii) – Dangerous Goods
            “Dangerous Goods mean goods which by reason of the nature, quantity or mode of storage of such goods are either
singly or collectively liable to endanger the life or the health of the persons within the port limits or on a vessel or to cause
damage to property within such port limits and includes such goods contained in a receptacle, portable tank, freight container or
vehicle as defined in the IMDG Code.  The term includes an empty receptacle, portable tank or tank vehicle which as been
previously used for carriage of dangerous goods unless such receptacle has been cleaned and dried or when the nature of the
former contents permits such carriage with safety and allow the containers to be closed securely.
Dangerous goods include all substance
(i)
                  Having properties coming within the classes listed in the IMDG Code;
(ii)                Substance defined as explosive as defined by the Explosive e Act, 1884 and /or the Explosive Rules, 1983;
(iii)               Any other goods which the competent authority may specify as dangerous goods;
(iv)              Hazardous chemicals listed in Schedule-1 of the Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemicals Rules,
1989”.
The regulation gives discretionary powers to the competent authority to specify and good as dangerous one.  Whether
such powers are exercised judiciously and are not liable to be misused?
Ministry’s reply
            Classification of the dangerous goods is based on International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code (IMDG Code). 
However, new types of hazardous chemicals are being manufactured, transported and traded.   Thus, Port may be called upon to
handle new chemicals before they are classified and listed under IMDG Code.  Hence, the Port has been vested with
discretionary powers to handle such chemicals.  However, these powers are exercised judiciously as the decision is based on the
chemical composition details of such goods obtained from the manufacturers and the importers/exporters.   Under the
circumstances Competent Authority has been assigned some discretionary powers.
Committee’s observation
The Committee noted the explanation given by the Ministry.

9)         Point Raised:-
 
Regulation 39:- Commutation
 
            "A pensioner may commute for a lump-sum payment, a fraction upto maximum of one-third of the pension admissible to
him. Such a pensioner will be entitled to the pension upto two-third portion of the admissible pension. Commuted portion of the
pension will be resorted after a period of fifteen years from the date of commutation. The method of commutation shall be in
accordance with the table enclosed hereto. If commutation is sought after one year of the ate of retirement, it will be granted
only after medical examination, by the Medical Officer of the Small Industries Bank."
 
            Under the provisions of this regulation, a pensioner may commute one-third of the admissible pension while under the
CCS (Pension) Rules, a pensioner may commute up to 40% of admissible pension. Whether Government have any objection in
maintaining parity in this regard?
 
            Ministry's Reply (01.07.03):-
 
            The subject regulation is exactly in line with similar such regulations applicable in IDBI and RBI. As SIDBI shares the
same parentage and as and when any revision in the Regulations of RBI and IDBI takes place, SIDBI will consider the same
principles for adoption.
 
            Committee's Observation (27.04.04):-
 
            The Committee was informed that the provision is exactly in line with the similar provision in IDBI and RBI Regulation.
The Committee desired the Ministry to review the relevant provisions of SIDBI, RBI and IDBI.
 
Action Taken by the Ministry (10.06.04):-
 
            The subject regulation has been adopted from IDBI. However, it is understood that RBI has made a reference to GoI for
increase in the commutation percentage to 40%. We propose to initiate necessary steps for the same.

4.         The Committee is, however, unhappy to note the shift in the Ministry’s stand from time to time while corresponding
with it on various points in the questionnaire; like point nos. 1, 2, 3, and 6, to mention a few. While the Committee agrees to
some extent to the Government’s logic to keep in line with the Pension Regulations of other financial institutions, but in that
case they should not act as an obstacle and retard the evolution in similar legislation that is taking place in other
institutions/organizations of Government.   For example, inclusion of part time workers within the definition of the term

statutory notifications and should not tend to postpone this work for the later part of the session so that the eventualities like early
prorogation of the House, which is of course rare, are taken care of.
 
 (ix) (A)    Ministry of Human Resource Development (Department of Higher Education)
 
The Committee notes with concern that the Ministry of Human Resource Development have delayed in laying notifications ranging from
5 months to 10 months.  The Ministry have also failed to append delay statements as well with their notification at (Sl. No. 114) (The
delay statement appended put forth the reason that these are being laid in the earliest Session after receipt of the documents from AICTE.
In future, all efforts will be made to ensure that these documents are laid on the Table of the House in time)
 
            The Committee notes with deep concern the inordinate delay in laying their notification of as much as 17 months.  The Committee
find that the laying of the notifications was delayed due to their late receipt in the Ministry from the AICTE. In this content the Committee
observes that it is the Ministry’s responsibility to ensure that the subordinate Legislation is laid before the Parliament within the prescribed
schedule and accordingly, it is for the Ministry only to ensure that they receive the same timely from the Statutory bodies under them .
The Committee recommends that the Department of Higher Education may take necessary remedial measures to ensure that papers are
received timely in the Ministry from the Statutory bodies.
(x)        Ministry of Labour & Employment (Directorate General of Employment & Training)
            The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Labour & Employment (Directorate General of Employment & Training)
have delayed by 5 months in laying their notification (Sl. No. 121).  Delay statement has been appended with the notification
            The Committee expects the Ministry of Labour & Employment (Directorate General of Employment& Training) to exercise
caution in the matter of timely laying of Subordinate Legislation and ensure that such delays do not recur.
(xi)       Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs
            The Committee notes with dismay that the Ministry have exceptionally delayed the laying of their notifications (Sl. Nos 130,131).
 
 
 
 
The delay in laying the said notifications ranges from 1 year to over 3 years.  The delay statement appended with GSR 143 dated
the 26
th February, 2004  and with  GSR 50 (E) dated 6 February, 2006 reads :
 
            “The work in respect of Emigration was transferred from Ministry of Labour to Indian Overseas Affairs. During this period six
notifications were issued in pursuance of the delegated power under the provisions of Emigration Act, 1983. The officers who monitor
Protector General of Emigration who regulates Emigration Act, 1983, and rules framed thereunder were transferred in haste as a result
thereof, these notifications could not be laid on the Table during this period.
 
            The Committee expresses its unhappiness over the inordinate delay that has taken place in the laying of the two notifications. The
reason for delay tendered by the Ministry do not seem to be very convincing, if seen with reference to the period of delay. The Committee,
accordingly, recommends that the Ministry should take all necessary precaution for future so as to avoid recurrence of such situations.
 
(xii)      Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions (Department of Personnel & Training)
 
            The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Personnel Public Grievances & Pensions (Department of Personnel &
Training) have delayed the laying of one of their notifications (Sl. No. 146) by ten months.  The delay statement appended with the said
notification reads:-
 
            “This notification had not been received in time from the Govt. of India Press due to this reason the same could not be laid on the
Table of Rajya Sabha within stipulated period.”
            The Committee would like to impress upon the Ministry of Personnel that it is their responsibility to ensure that copies of the
notifications are received timely from the Government of India Press and for this purpose they may evolve a suitable mechanism of
check/counter check so that such instances do no recur. The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Personnel would take action
accordingly in order to comply with the prescribed schedule in the matter of laying of Statutory notifications.
 
(xiii)      Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas

The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas have delayed by 6 months the laying of their

            The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas should take necessary remedial steps to ensure that the

(xiv)     Ministry of Power   
 
            The Committee regrets to note that one notification (Sl. No. 160) laid by the Ministry of Power has been delayed by seven

            The Committee hopes that the Ministry would avoid such instances of delay in laying of Subordinate Legislation in future. The
Committee also impress upon the Ministry to take note of the fact that in case there is a delay in the laying of any Statutory notification,
the same should be accompanied by a delay statement while it is being laid.
 
           
(xv)      Ministry of Urban Development
 
            The Committee notes with serious concern that the Ministry of Urban Development have delayed the laying of their notification
(Sl.No. 186) abnormally by 1 year and 3 months.  The delay statement appended to the notification reads;
 
“Copies of the Gazette Notification were received in the Ministry from the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) on 21.11.2006,
and reason for delay was received from DDA on 11.12.2006.  The delay in furnishing the copies of the Gazette Notification by DDA
occurred due to administrative lapses on the part of DDA officials. Suitable action against the defaulting officials is being taken.
 
            The Recruitment Regulations for the post of Asstt. Engineer (Civil/Electrical) in DDA were proposed to be laid on the Table of
both the Houses of Parliament during the winter Session 2006.  However, by the time the papers were ready for laying, the Winter Session
2006 had concluded.  Delay caused in laying these Notifications on the Table of the Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha is regretted.”
 
 
 
The Committee recommends the Ministry of Urban Development to adhere strictly to the schedule as recommended by the
Committee for timely laying of Subordinate Legislation.   The Committee hopes that the Ministry would be able to avoid recurrence of
such instances in future.
 
 
3.     The Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/Departments to take immediate steps to ensure timely and proper laying of
subordinate legislation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Departments of the Government of
India, particularly, the defaulting ones, the following recommendations, as contained in its 131
st,135th  and 152nd Reports:
        “Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session immediately
following the date of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Session, on the date of the publication of
the Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between the date of publication and the date of the closing of the Session is less
than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the Session immediately following the said Session. All the Ministries/Departments of
Government of India should henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of the Orders issued under various Acts of
Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.” (131

prescribed by the Committee and whether such notifications were accompanied by a statement indicating the
reasons for the delay in laying. In some of the cases the delay has been quite long. The
observations/recommendations of the Committee in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments are as follows:
-  
         
(i)        Ministry of Agro & Rural Industries 
 
          The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of 11 months and 9 months, respectively, in
laying of two notifications (Sl Nos. 1 & 2) and no delay statement was sent therewith.
 
          The Committee would like the Ministry of Agro & Rural Industries to take corrective measures so as to
obviate such delay in future and in case such delays occur the notification while being laid before Parliament
should be accompanied  by statutes giving reason for the delay in laying.
    
(ii)     Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Department of Commerce)
 
          The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Department of Commerce)
have delayed the laying of their notification (Sl. No. 4) by 3 months. The delay statement appended by the said
notification reads:-
 
          “The Coffee Board (Cadre & Recruitment) Rules, 1993 were framed by the Coffee Board in accordance with
the powers conferred by Rule 31 of the Coffee Board Rules, 1955.  As there was no provision under Rule 31 of the
Coffee Rules, 1955 regarding laying of the rules made thereunder, on the table of the Parliament, the same could
not be laid on the Table of each House of Parliament.
 
          However, the Rajya Sabha Committee on Subordinate Legislation were of the view that as per sub-section
(xv) of Section 48 of the Coffee Act, 1942, the rule making powers, in respect of Pay & allowances, leave and
other conditions of the service of the staff employed by the Board (other than those appointed by Central Govt.)
and other employees of the Board, are vested with the Central Govt. and as
such these rules should have been framed by the Central Govt. not by the Coffee Board.”
           The Committee regrets to note that the delay statement gives only the circumstance under which the
required rules have framed/laid but there is nothing in it to explain how the laying of the notification has been
delayed by three months.  The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Department of
Commerce) would take note of discrepancy and avoid recurrence of the same in future.
 
 
(iii)              Ministry of Communications & Information Technology (Department of Information
Technology)
 
          The Committee notes with regret that there has been a delay of 10 months in laying of one notification (
Sl.No.7) and no delay statement was sent therewith.
         
          The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Communications & Information Technology (Department
of Information Technology) should strictly adhere to the time schedule as recommended by it and in case there is a
delay in laying the notification should invariably be accompanied by a delay statement explaining the reasons for
such delay.
 
(iv)              Ministry of Consumer affairs Food & Public Distribution (Department of Consumer Affairs)

Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, particularly, the defaulting ones, the following
recommendations, as contained in its 131st,135th  and 152nd Reports:
      “Orders required to be laid before the House should be laid (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session
immediately following the date of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in
Session, on the date of the publication of the Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between the
date of publication and the date of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the
Session immediately following the said Session. All the Ministries/Departments of Government of India should
henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of the Orders issued under various Acts of Parliament
on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.
(131st Report)
(Presented on 15 December 2000)
      “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized that it is essential that in case there is a delay in the laying of
Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Department should invariably append a delay statement along with the
notifications being laid so as to apprise Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee desires all
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, since the intension is that through the process of formulation of a
delay statement the Ministry is able to introspect, identify bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”.
(135
th Report)
(Presented on 27 July 2001)
 
      “In the opinion of the Committee, every notification should be assigned a distinctive number in order to give it
a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be published/laid which does not carry a notification
number. The Committee expects all Ministries/Departments of Government of India to exercise caution in this
regard. In case where there are more than one notification under a single file, the Ministries/Departments should
ensure that the file number on each notification should be suitably distinguished from one another.
(152nd Report)

The term “Edible Oils” does not include ghee and butter, as ghee and butter are of animal origin and not of vegetable

(1)     Point referred
          Whether the Bombay Port (Licensing and Control of Pilots) Regulations, 1975 have since been laid on the Table
of both the Houses and if, so the date of laying thereof.
Ministry’s reply
          When these regulations were framed in 1975, there was no provision in the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 for
placing of regulations before both Houses of Parliament.  This requirement was introduced by insertion of provision by
Act 17 of 1982 with effect from 31.5.1982.
Committee’s observation
          The Committee was appraised that the regulations were not laid on the table of both the Houses as there was no
laying provision in the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 prior to 1982.  The Committee desired that the regulations should
be laid now alongwith the amendments suggested by it.
(2)     Point referred: Regulation 1 (2)
          “They shall come into force on the date of the publication of the Government’s sanction in the Official Gazette.”
          Generally the rules/regulations are brought into effect from the date of publication of the Official Gazette. What
is the significance of publication of “Government’s sanction” in case of the rules in hand?
Ministry’s reply
          Section 124 (1) of the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 provides that no regulation made by the Board under the Act
(other than a regulation made under sub-section 2 of section 17) shall have effect until it has been approved by the
Central Government and until such approval has been published in the Official Gazette.   The provision in the
regulation is accordingly worded for the regulations to come into effect from date of publication of Government’s
sanction in the Gazette.   In effect, however, the regulations came into effect from the date of publication in the
Gazette.
Committee’s observation
          The management of the board had agreed to amend the commencement clause as suggested by the Committee.
(3)     Point referred: Regulation 3 - Definitions
          The term “pilot” is generally associated with the aeroplanes .  But here it has been used for handling of vessels. 
Whether Government have any objection in inserting the definition of word “Pilot” in the regulation itself?
Ministry’s reply
          The term ‘Pilot’ is defined in the Indian Ports Act, 1908, section 3 (3) as under:
          ‘Pilot’ means a person for the time being authorized by Government to pilot vessels.”
          It is a term in the standard international maritime vocabulary.  Hence, it is not included in the definition in the

6.       Point raised
Schedule-III
For appointment to the posts in the Schedule, the method of promotion has been stated to be on the basis of
seniority-cum-merit.
What are the main features of this procedure for promotion; Whether it is permissible to change the seniority of
officials as it exists in the feeder grade while recommending their names for promotion to the next higher grade which
is inherent in the “selection” as a method of promotion at least for the purpose of promotion in scale III, scale II and
scale I so as to promote merit in the organisation?
Ministry’s reply
“Seniority-cum-merit” shall mean seniority and found fit for promotion.   It is not possible to change the
seniority of officials, as it exists in the feeder grade.  Thus, seniority-cum-merit implies promotions based on seniority
subject to minimum necessary merit requisite for the promotion.  The Government feels that there should be a uniform
criterion for promotion to all scales and that the present system may continue.
Committee’s Observation
The Committee came across divergent views on the point of promotion on the basis of seniority-cum-merit.  The
Bank of Rajasthan was of the view that promotion should not be purely on the basis of seniority only and merit should
also be given at least 50% weight age.  The Dungarpur Banswara Gramin Bank was of the view that in lower scales,
weight age may be given to seniority but in higher scale merit should prevail.   The Gramin Bank was of the view that
promotion should be made on the basis of both seniority and merit.  The Committee reiterated the need for balance
between seniority and merit to keep the Regional Rural Banks competitive with the other commercial banks.
Action taken
The existing recruitment rules provide for filling up the posts by seniority-cum-merit.   It, therefore, gives due
weightage to the seniority as well as merit.    However, the position would be reviewed after the process for
amalgamation is completed.

Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules-2002
 
          The Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002 framed under the Securitisation  & Reconstruction of
Financial Assets & Enforcement of Security Interest Ordinance, 2002 were examined and a questionnaire was
forwarded to the Ministry of Finance (Banking Division) on the 24th November, 2003, to which the Ministry replied
on the 7th May, 2004. The Committee considered the Ministry’s reply at its meeting held on 17 th November, 2005
and decided to seek further clarification on point No.1 (Rule 2 (d) defining ‘Approved Valuer’). The Ministry vide
their communication dated 29 th November, 2006 provided the requisite clarification and also gave details of the
changes carried out by the Ministry on the other points on Committee’s suggestion.
 
2.       The points referred to the Ministry, their comments/clarifications and their Action Taken on each point are
reproduced below: -
 
1.       Point raised- Rule 2(d) -
“Approved valuer” means a valuer  as approved by the Board of Directors or Board of Trustees of the
secured creditor, as the case may be.
Should the approved valuer  not be duly qualified; what is the justification for giving full discretion to the
secured creditor in this regard?
 
          Ministry’s 
comments : (7.5. 2004)
Approved valuer means the professional who is qualified to value the property for a fee.  It is difficult to
work out clear-cut definition making exhaustive list of approved valuers  in different fields and types of properties
that are to be valued.   It is, however, suggested that banks and financial institutions may be advised to utilize the
services of valuers through Institution of Valuers  who claimed to be the only registered body in the country and
their members are bound by code of conduct prescribed by it.  They are covered by fee prescribed by the
Government under Rule 8C of the Wealth Tax Act and also by CBDT.
 
 
Action Taken by the 
Ministry : (29.11.2006)
In terms of Rule 8(5) of Security Enforcement Rules, 2002, before effecting sale of immovable property, the
authorized officer is required to obtain valuation of the property from an approved valuer and in consultation with
the secured creditor, fix the reserve price of the property.  Chapter VII-B (Section 34 AB) of Wealth Tax Act, 1957

provides for registration of valuers.  Any person who possesses the qualifications prescribed under Rule 8A of
Wealth Tax Rules, 1957, may apply to the Chief Commissioner or Director General for being registered as a valuer

          Ministry’s 
comments : (7.5. 2004)
Witnesses could be any one.  Flexibility in this matter is desirable and is recognized by the legislation as well
as judiciary.   No clarification in the Rule is necessary, as the present provision does not confine witnesses to
specific classes of persons.

The authorized officer shall keep the property taken possession under sub-rules (1) either in his own custody
or in the custody of any person authorized or appointed by him, who shall take as much care of the property in his
custody as an owner of ordinary prudence would, under the similar circumstances, take of such property.
                            
 
This rule involves further delegation of power by the authorized officer to any person authorized or appointed
by him without fixing any responsibility either to the authorized officer or the person so authorized or appointed by
him in case there is any damage to the movable property in custody inadvertently.   Should the rule not vest ultimate
responsibility on the authorised officer even in case where he has authorized some body in this behalf?
 
Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)

of ordinary prudence.  Further as per Rule 4(4), the Authorised Officer shall take steps for preservation and
protection of secured assets and insure them, if necessary, till they are sold or otherwise disposed of.  Therefore
even though the Authorised Officer is empowered to entrust the possession to others; he is still responsible for acts
of the custodian appointed by him to keep the assets.  Moreover, in terms of Section 19 of the Act, if the DRT or
DRAT holds the possession of secured assets by the secured creditor as wrongful and directs the secured creditor to

Valuation of movable secured assets: After taking possession under sub-rule (1) of the Rule 4 and

objection in defining them in the regulations it or whether any other set of regulations will be framed for the

Ministry’s Comments

          IRDA has reported that details of number of posts, their classification, scale of pay, age limit,
education and other qualification, period of probation, method of recruitment, composition of selection
committee of departmental selection committee have not been mentioned in the regulations as these will
form part of administrative orders to be issued from time to time. The Insurance Advisory Committee which

'merit' and seniority are the words that are used; what is the justification for deviations from general

Ministry’s Comments
:- (14/03/2002)
          IRDA has reported that word "suitability" has been included deliberately in the regulations as a

          The Ministry have stated that the Small Industries Development Bank of India Pension Regulations,
1993 were not notified. The Committee desired to know the justification for not notifying the said
regulations.
 
          Ministry’s further Comments (13.06.05):-
 
          SIDBI was created out of IDBI w.e.f. April 02, 1990 as per SIDBI Act, 1989. Since its formation,
SIDBI is following the service regulations and all other rules relating to the service matters as that of IDBI.
IDBI Pension Regulations were notified in 1995 and have been made applicable w.e.f. November 01, 1993.
In terms of the sixth bi-partie settlement between the IBA and the unions/associations of the bank
employees, the pension scheme was introduced in the nationalized banks w.e.f. November 01, 1993, but
notified in 1995. SIDBI also formulated the Pension Regulations in 1993 in anticipation of approval of the
Government. During the course of the consideration of the pension regulations, the question of constituting
Pension Fund had arisen and it was considered that since SIDBI had been granted tax exemption, there may
not be any need of constituting a separate Pension Fund. On further consideration of the matter, it was felt
to explore the possibility of adopting the pattern of RBI & NABARD Employee Gratuity and
Superannuation Fund Regulations instead of having a separate Pension Regulations in line with IDBI,
which had become a tax paying corporate entity. It, therefore, necessitated an exercise afresh to draft the
SIDBI Employee Gratuity and Superannuation Fund Regulations in line with RBI Regulations. Due to the
above development and subsequent developments like divestment of shares of IDBI in SIDBI and other
allied developments, the Pension Regulations of SIDBI were revisited and SIDBI Pension Regulations,
2002 were notified. It may be pertinent to mention that due to the late notification of the SIDBI Pension
Regulations, the employees have not been affected in any manner as the said Pension Regulations cover
employees from the date of creation of SIDBI subject to fulfillment of conditions.

      The Determination of the Price of the Forfeited Property Rules, 2005  
 
 The Determination of the Price of the Forfeited Property Rules, 
2005 framed under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 were 
examined and certain points, which needed further 
comments/clarifications, were put together in the form of a questionnaire. 
It was forwarded to the Ministry of Home Affairs for their 
comments/clarifications on July 10, 2006.  In reply, the Ministry of Home 
Affairs vide their communication dated October 16, 2006 informed as 
follows :- 
“….that the comments of Rajya Sabha Secretariat 
were examined and draft   comments were sent to the 
Ministry of Law for vetting.  The Ministry of Law has 
accepted the comments of Ministry of Home Affairs in Rule 
6.  The Comments in Rule 3, 5(1), 5(2), 7(1) and 7(2) have 
been reexamined and fresh comments of this Ministry are 
enclosed. 
 
On receipt of the Rajya Sabha acceptance on the 
proposed comments/amendments, the approval of Hon’ble 
Home Minister will be obtained for notifying the same.” 
 
2. The   points   referred to the Ministry and their comments thereon 
are reproduced below : 
 
1.     Point raised:  Rule 3 : Appointment of Authorised Officer  
“Where the person against whom an order of forfeiture has been 
made (hereinafter referred to as the person), is acquitted, the property 
shall  be returned to him or his legal nominee and if it is not possible for 
any reason to return the forfeited property, the State Government shall 

appoint an officer not below the rank of Deputy Secretary to that 
Government, to be known as Authorised Officer, to evaluate and fix the 
price of the forfeited property with a view to compensating the person in 
lieu of the forfeited property.” 
As per Rule 3, all what has been said about the Authorised Officer 
is that he must not be below the rank of Deputy Secretary of the 
Government. As the job of evaluation is technical, should the Authorised 
Officer not possess some technical qualification also? 
 
 
Ministry's reply: 
In order to have a more cogent procedure for the authorized officer 
to compute the value of forfeited property, it is proposed that Rule 3 
may be amended by inserting an explanation which will allow the 
Authorized Officer to utilize the service of consultant(s)/Valuer(s) to 
arrive at the value of forfeited property. 
 
2.    Point raised: Rule 5 : Consideration of the representation : 
          "(1) The Authorised Officer shall take into account, representation, 
if any, made by the person or his leg al nominee before the final 
determination of the price with respect to the forfeited property is made" 
 Whether the Ministry have any objection in specifying a time frame 
for disposal of representation, if any, given by the person or his legal 
nominee or f or that matter for completing the whole process of 
determining the price of the forfeited property under the rules? 
 
Ministry's reply 

 180 days from the first day of the next month of the receipt of the 
representation. 
 
3.    Point raised: Rule 5: Consideration of the representation: 
 
          "(2) The Authorised Officer shall thereafter fix the price of the 
forfeited property and intimate the same in writing to the person or his 
legal nominee". 
 Rule 5 mentions that the Authorised Officer shall intimate the person 
or his legal nominee as to the fixing of the price of the forfeited property. 
Rule 6 maintains that the State Government should issue an order to the 
effect that the property stands sold to the State Government at the price 
fixed under rule 5. 
        Whether the intimation to the person/legal nominee is accompanied 
by such an order, or such an arrangement is being viewed as an assurance 
to the concerned individual. 
Ministry's reply: 
 Within 60 days from the date the proces s of determining the price of 
forfeited property is completed. 
 The persons/legal nominee is informed about the price of the forfeited 
property as per Rule 5(2) of the said Act. Further reference by the State 
Government to the Central Government about the Head of Account etc. 
is an administrative function only.  The M/o Law and Justice have opined 
that this appears to be sustainable. 
 
4.    Point raised : Rule 7: Deposit of the amount by the Central 
Government: 
 

           " (1) The Central Government shall on receipt of the order under 
rule 6, deposit the price fixed for the forfeited property in such Treasury 
or under such Head of Account as may be specified therein under 
intimation to the person or his legal nominee." 
 As the matter being of utmost urgency  to the affected individual, 
whether the Ministry have any objection in specifying a time -frame 
within which the Central Government, after receipt of such an order as 
specified in rule 6, deposit the forfeited property in such Treasury under 
such Head of A ccount as specified in such an order under intimation to 
the person or his legal nominee.   
 
Ministry's reply: 
 Within 30 days from the date of order as specified in Rule 6. 
 
5.    Point raised: Rule 7: Deposit of the amount by the Central 
Government: 
 
           " (2) The amount of price along with interest there on, shall be paid 
to the person  
Or to his legal nominee."  
   
           Sub-rule (2) of Rule 7 mentioned about payment of the price of the 
forfeited property along with "interest thereon". Wheth er Ministry will 
specify at what rate interest will be paid to the claimant? 
 
 
 
Ministry's reply: 

 It is proposed that the interest may be paid at the prevailing interest 
rates on savings bank account of State Bank of India.  
 
The Committee considered the replies of the Ministry of Home 
Affairs on the points forwarded to them.  The Committee notes with 
satisfaction that the Ministry of Home Affairs have agreed to take action 
as follows in pursuance to its suggestions : 
(i) In Rule 3, to insert  an explanation allowing  the Authorized 
Officer to utilize the service of consultant(s)/Valuer(s) to 
arrive at the value of forfeited property.  In the existing rules, 
the Authorised Officer is required to do this job  without any  
assistance; and   
(ii) In Rule  7 (2), to  make provision for paying  the interest at 
the prevailing interest rates on savings bank account of State 
Bank of India on the price of the forfeited property to the 
claimant.  The existing provisions do no mention about  the 
rate of interest. 
 The Committee hopes that the Ministry would carry out the above 
amendments expeditiously under intimation to it. However, on other 
points, the Committee notes with satisfaction the reply given by  the 
Ministry of Home Affairs.
